body:
If you read last week's blog, you might recall that I had a "Cautious" outlook for the market this week, as I believed the jump in oil prices and U.S./Iran re-escalation was not being fully discounted by investors. At the time of this writing (1:34 p.m. ET) all the majors are on track to be down modestly on the week, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq  Composite being the worst performer (-1.4%). The exchange of attacks between the U.S. and Iran continued this week and oil prices continued to climb [...] Loading navigation

# Weekly Trader's Outlook

## Middle East Tensions, Rising Oil & Yields Weigh on Stocks

Stocks are on track for modest weekly losses, particularly in the technology space, as rising oil prices and higher Treasury yields keep investors sidelined, despite strong earnings reports.

July 24, 2026•Nathan Peterson

## The Week That Was [...] Thursday (July 30): Continuing Claims, EIA Natural Gas Inventories, Q2 GDP – Advanced Reading, Initial Claims, PCE Prices, Personal Income, Personal Spending
 Friday (July 31): Chicago PMI, Employment Cost Index, University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment

May 18, 2026

Inflation is being temporarily lifted by energy supply shocks and Europe's early outperformance has faded in 2026, but we still see potential opportunities ahead as U.S. equities enter the summer with a constructive outlook and strong momentum.

May 11, 2026

The stakes are high on the eve of the U.S.-China summit. Meanwhile, a narrow rebound could mask broad-based earnings growth and Artificial Intelligence is increasingly driving market leadership. [...] July 20, 2026

We believe the appointment of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh has strengthened confidence in price stability. The durability of broader U.S. equity leadership could depend on containing inflation and Federal Reserve policy pressure.

July 13, 2026

Amid high analyst expectations for upcoming Q2 earnings reports, we believe the U.S. economy remains resilient and the Federal Reserve seems likely to remain in a holding pattern.

July 6, 2026 [...] May 26, 2026

While markets signal resilient growth and strong earnings, rising energy-driven inflation and surging Treasury yields are tightening financial conditions. Meanwhile, it may be time to rethink Emerging Markets as a single coherent asset class.

May 18, 2026

Against this backdrop, we remain neutral duration relative to the benchmark. However, we are raising our expected range for where the 10-year Treasury may trade over the remainder of the year to 4.5%–5.0% (from 4.0%–4.5%), reflecting both renewed energy-driven inflation pressures from the U.S.–Iran conflict and the Fed’s heightened sensitivity to upside inflation surprises.

### AI narratives remain in the driver's seat for stocks [...] We believe rising oil prices and higher yields represent an emerging risk that could influence the Fed’s policy path in the months ahead and contribute to greater market volatility as we head into the seasonally softer August and September period. However, underlying economic and corporate fundamentals remain constructive, in our view, supporting a cautiously optimistic outlook for the back half of the year. [...] A fresh round of escalation in the U.S.–Iran conflict is driving oil back toward the early June highs, reversing much of the progress made after the April ceasefire and the June 17 Memorandum of Understanding. Energy markets have, to some extent, defied earlier fears of a sharper spike, with countries drawing down inventories, softer Chinese demand, and alternative shipping routes helping keep supply flowing.
